Three of us signed up for the plane ride about a month in advance. There were really high winds that day (40 mph+), but the company didn't cancel so we went for the ride. 15 minutes in, another passenger started vomiting. Somehow the three of us survived the turbulence, which took all of the fun out of the amazing views and great narrations. About 30 minutes in we were wishing it was over- the turbulence was intolerable and quite frightening, and making us so sick we were doing all we could not to vomit. After getting off the plane we were so nauseated that we had to lay down at the airport for about an hour before getting back in the car. Go on a calm day- not worth the cost to be sick in a tiny plane in high winds.

We made reservations for our airplane flight less than 2 weeks out via the website. We remembered to call more than 24 hours in advance to confirm our flight. Our flight departed on time and we had incredible views of the canyon. Our pilot was very friendly and rather humorous. Our plane was small and seated 8, so everyone had a window seat in order to observe the Grand Canyon. I would use this airline again and would recommend them to others. 

We had one little hiccup, which the company took care of without too much trouble. According to the reservation paperwork, guests can pay $10 extra for a guaranteed window seat. When we called to confirm our reservation we asked to guarantee the window seats. They said they could only take a "request" at that time and made note in their system. When we checked in for the flight, I inquired into our request. I was told that our plane was an 8 seater and a all seats were window seats, which was great. But then they requested that we pay the additional $10 per person because we had requested the seats... even though EVERYONE would have a window seat. Again, they did remove the "request" from our reservation and all was good, but it was a little frustrating for a minute. Thankfully they did the right thing.

One thing to note - the men's bathroom was under construction when we visited (June 9, 2013) and all male guests had to use the port-a-potties outside. I was very thankful that the women's bathroom was fully functional!

review_title: A highlight of our Grand Canyon visit
review_text:
OK so I'm a bit biased because I like light aircraft flights, much better than soulless airliners. An aerial view of the Grand Canyon is a must see, we got some great photos as well as just sitting back enjoying the view and I suspect you would not see any more from a pricier helicopter flight.

As to the organisation, efficient, amiable, no delays; the aircraft was full but there was plenty of room (and I'm tall) with no restrictions on the views.

The Grand Canyon lives up to the hype and this flight enhanced the experience.

review_title: Une vue imprenable sur le Grand Canyon
review_text: Même si désormais les avions offrent 3 places de front, la vue par les larges hublots est parfaite. Les commentaires associées complètent les superbes vues car les vols ne sont effectués que dans de bonnes conditions météo. L'aérodrome est de plus tout à côté du Grand Canyon National Park. De plus le prix demeure abordable !

Wow, what an amazing trip! Nothing compares to that experience, really. We just took the 45 min tour from the South Rim airport. Checking in went smooth and the staff was friendly. The ride itself was just incredible. Those views are remarkable. If you're visiting the Grand Canyon, please don't skip this attraction.

review_title: The best way to see the Grand Canyon
review_text: This is a review of the Scenic Airlines - Grand Canyon National Park. We took the 45 minute flight in an aeroplane, which is the same cost as a 20 minute flight in a helicopter. The flight takes you all of the way around the Grand Canyon. We were lucky to chose a perfect day in terms of weather, calm, sunny and blue sky. The flight is great, it gives you a really good perspective of the Grand Canyon. its comfortable, relatively quiet the plane takes approx 18 -21 passengers. Excellent views from all seats, there are 3 in each row, two by window either side and one in the middle, all get great views. If you're going all the way to the Grand Canyon, these operate from the South rim airport, don't miss this opportunity as well as walking in and around the Canyon. This beats all the views you get walking and helps give you an idea of the scale of the place. Its awesome and breathtaking. Thanks for a great flight, it was the highlight of our two day visit to the Grand Canyon. Remember to book online beforehand for the best price.

I took the Indian Country With Skywalk tour on March 20th.  They were waiting outside of my Las Vegas hotel right on time.  After a pleasant ride to Boulder City Airport, we waited a short while before boarding a clean and comfortable 19-passenger DeHavilland DHC-6-300 plane. The plane ride was very nice to the Grand Canyon West airport, passing over the dam along the way.  From there we were able to take the hop-on-hop-off buses to the two stops included with tour.  Both places offered wonderful views of the canyon, with the Skywalk at one and a tasty lunch at the other. Lots of fantastic photo opportunities along the edge of a 4000-foot drop!  The pilots and ground crew were all very pleasant. I would gladly do it again.

Hermoso paseo para conocer la inmensidad del cañón, se aprecia una vista totalmente diferente que desde la pasarela.
Todo funciono perfecto, desde la reserva online, envió de voucher y salida en horario. El tour tiene audio en distintos idiomas que comentan datos del cañón.
Muy recomendable!

Une des façons les plus émouvantes de parcourir des yeux la magnificence du lieu , avec comme point d'orgue le point de partage des eaux entre le " Petit Colorado " à la livrée turquoise , et le fleuve roi aux nuances émeraude ...

review_title: Grand Canyon national park airplane/ground tour
review_text: Fabulous day! The staff were outstanding from pick up to drop off, they were a delightful team who's enthusiasm was infectious.  The South rim of the Canyon is a little further to fly but the views are breathtaking.  2 hours are spent on the ground split into 2 park viewing  areas.  This trip wets the thirst for return holidays! The views from the air (1 hour each way) are spectacular!!!

Nous avons fait le highlight tour en avion il y a quelques jours et nous en reparlons chaque jour des étoiles plein les yeux. 

Nous avons été enchantés de notre trip : d'abord un petit shuttle est venu nous chercher à notre hotel pour nous emmener à l'aéroport de Boulder City.
Nous étions une petite dizaine a bord. 

Arrivés sur place, pas de cohue : 4 guichets ouverts où l'on vous pese (très discrètement), vérifie vos passeports et vous attribue une couleur.
Nous avons attendu 20 min entre l'enregistrement et le moment où nous avons embarqué.

Devant l'avion, le pilote vous explique les consignes de sécurité et vous attribue un siège.
Il y a 10 places, le pilote compris, et chacun a sa fenêtre.
Un casque est à votre disposition avec des explications, dans différents langues, dont en français.

Lors du décollage, ca secoue pas mal ; mais une fois dans les airs, le paysage vous coupe tellement le souffle que vous ne prêtez plus attention aux secousses.

Que vous dire de la vue, si ce n'est que c'est magnifique et que c'est une des plus belles choses que nous n'ayons jamais vu ?!!!
Franchement, allez-y sans crainte et profitez de chaque instant.

Le vol a duré 1h10 et le prix est clairement justifié.

We took a tour with Alan from the South Rim to Glen Canyon where we continued with Smooth Water Rafting on the Colorado River.  He picked us up at Lee's Ferry and we continued our tour back to the South Rim.  Alan was a wealth of knowledge and our trip was perfect.  He is an awesome tour guide; we learned so much and his pleasant and courteous personality is a gift.

We were initially a bit disappointed when the helicopter tours were booked out and opted for a fixed-wing Highlights tour instead. Good move! We saw much more of the canyon when we did a helicopter tour a few years ago, and loved every minute of it. The staff - both on the phone, at the counter and the aircrew - are fantastic. Without exception, they are courteous, friendly and very helpful.  I would have no hesitation whatsoever in recommending this tour - well done Scenic!!

We were booked for a tour to the south rim but because of the shut down we couldn't go. Scenic airline were brilliant and altered our tour to fly to the west rim which was still open. The whole experience was incredible and very well organised. Many thanks

Seeing the Grand Canyon from the air during a 40 minute journey in a small aircraft was exhilarating to say the least, plus it gave you a real sense as to how big it actually is. At 10 miles long and 270 miles wide it is enormous.
A word of advice though. Try to do it on a still day. When we did it the wind was gusty and the plane bobbed about quite a bit!!!! Not for those with tender stomachs !!

We decided to spring for the Canyon River Adventure as part of our western US National Parks tour and were so glad we did!!  It was a long day (12 hrs) but so worth it.  It began with a dawn flight over and through the Grand Canyon - awesome colors and views!!  Next came Antelope Canyon - a little known treasure on an Indian reservation.  This narrow walk-thru canyon is filled with spectacular colored rock and there are no words to express it.  Finally, we had a motorized raft ride down the Colorado River from Glen Canyon dam to Lee's Landing.  No serious rapids on this section of the river but prepare to get wet on the smaller "riffles."  This trip was worth every penny so don't err on the side of cheap.  Book it!!

review_title: Do it, do it!! Incredible service and great tour!
review_text:
I am terrified of flying and was really dreading the Grand Canyon tour.
 As we drove to Boulder airport I was becoming more and more terrified. As I walked into the airport a lovely lady who worked there greeted us and I started crying I was that scared. She was absolutely lovely she asked me if I am scared flying. I informed her I was and I was not sure if I could go ahead with it. She said this happens to a lot of people and if I go and check in and have a seat she will come back and have a chat with me.

After I checked in she came back, sat down next to me, explained that the plane is very safe, the pilots are fully qualified, if the conditions aren't safe they won't fly etc. She was so lovely, she gave me a hug and some vouchers for a free drink and a souvenir photo. I felt so much more at ease just by someone talking to me and I am SO glad I went through with it.

I did not get the lady's name during my mini meltdown but I thank her from the bottom of my heart. I did the tour on Saturday 5th October and arrived at the airport very early in the morning before sunrise.

We did the skywalk and had lunch overlooking the Grand Canyon. I was blown away. One of the true wonders of the world. No photos can do it justice.

We thoroughly enjoyed our tour which only cost about $150 which we thought was very good value.
Hotel pick up/drop off service was handy, but very time consuming.  Our one hour flight turned into a 5 hour excursion.
Can definately recommend the sunset tour time - the setting sun made the desert and canyon look amazing.

review_title: Great tour of South Rim - Transportation from airport needs work
review_text:
My wife and I plus three other family members took the Grand Canyon Connoisseur trip from Las Vegas to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon on September 30th and had a great trip.  We were picked up on time on the Strip, transported to the Boulder City Airport and then flew to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon Nat'l Park.  Excellent box lunch was provided and we were bused to several viewing points in the Grand Canyon Village, where we spent 2 1/2 hours.  Both the flight and bus trip within the National Park were narrated for key points.  We had a great pilot and very smooth  trip on the 70 minute flight each way.  The Grand Canyon South Rim is breathtaking and something that everyone should try to see in person.  

The problem after the return to the Boulder City airport is there were no representatives from Grand Canyon Tours at the airport to insure you got assigned on a shuttle bus back to Las Vegas.  It took us 2 1/2 hours to get back from the Airport, which is normally only a 40 minute trip.  Better work and staffing by Scenic Airlines/Grand Canyon Tours at Boulder City Airport would make this a 5 star trip.

Tip to Travellers - Make sure you get a Bus Pass at the Transportation Desk immediately upon your return to Boulder City Airport for the included free shuttle back to the Vegas hotels.

Super ervaring! Ik vond het geweldig vanaf het moment dat je incheckt totdat je weer naar buiten loopt. Fijne ontvangst door een hele vriendelijke mevrouw aan de balie. Inchecken...wegen...boarden...en we kregen gelukkig onze window seats! Inclusief nederlands gesproken geluid op onze koptelefoon. De vlucht duurde 45min, tijdens de vlucht informatie over (het ontstaan van) de Grand Canyon, afgewisseld door muziek. Vooraf wordt er nog een leuke foto gemaakt van jou met de piloot en het vliegtuigje en je bent toerist dus natuurlijk koop je die bij terugkomst. Tip: vanaf thuis al boeken!

review_title: Longer day than expected with lots of waiting around.
review_text: I think the only way to see the Grand Canyon is to fly, either by plane or helicopter. We didnt fancy a 14hr bus tour and for the extra price I definately think the flight was worth it even though there was a lot of waiting around. We were picked up at 6am for a 8am flight, it took an hour to drive out to their airstrip in Boulder City and then had an hour to wait for our flight. All seemed to run smoothly until it was time to board our returning flight at 12.15pm, it was such a schmozzle the pilots didnt know who was on what flight, They let people that had been on later morning flights board planes before those that had been on earlier ones. Needless to say we ended up having to wait another 2hrs before we could finally board our flight.To top this off, when returning back to Boulder City we had to wait another 40mins for our transfers back to Las Vegas. Lots of waiting around with this tour that could have been avoided if the company was a bit more organised. Would recommend it but only because it's better then the alternative bus tour.

review_title: Great value for a Grand Canyon 'must'.
review_text:
Booked the Grand Discovery plane tour (through Papillon) for a 9am flight. The check-in staff and pilot were friendly and we boarded with minimal fuss. The tour itself was a 45 minute flight, and we had an 8-seater plane. The high wings and seat placing meant everyone gets an uninterrupted view, which I thought was brilliant! The guided audio tour is fine, with some information interspersed between music - you can choose not to listen though. 

The views are stunning and the plane tour, which was the cheapest flight over the Canyon we could find, was an excellent way of seeing the Canyon on a lower budget.

Vol dans un petit avion de 8 places ou tout le monde a son hublot, génial ! Accueil très sympatique, photo avec le pilote et c est parti pour 1 heure de pur bonheur.  Vues a couper le souffle, grandioses, magiques. Tout le monde est équipe d un casque avec commentaires dans la langue de votre choix. On en a vraiment pour notre argent. A faire impérativement si on va au grand canyon

Checked in at 8:15am for a 9:00am flight. They weighed us and gave us our seat assignments. 1 seat on the left side, 2 seats on the right side of the aircraft (Twin Otter). I asked about getting a seat on the left side (heard it was better). The agent said that because we had children, we needed to be seated next to them, thus, we'd be on the right side. I was disappointed, but hey, it sounds reasonable to me.

The crew offer a picture in front of the airplane before boarding. On board, we are given a quick safety brief and shown where the barf bags are. They have headset over which a guided tour is played during the flight.

The right side of the airplane is just fine for viewing the canyon and surrounding areas. I certainly didn't feel cheated. The windows are big and you can see out of either side. Note: if you are seat in row 4, the wing strut will be in the middle of your field of view. Not a deal breaker, but something to consider.

The canned tour was of poor quality and after about twenty minutes, I just took the headsets off so I could speak to my son.

Great flight and nice landing.

They try to sell you the photo at the end of the tour. It is a decent photo of your family surrounded by a collage of Grand Canyon images. Not my cup of tea, so we didn't spend the $20.

IMPORTANT: On your online reservation email, read the terms and conditions! You must call prior to showing up to RE-confirm that you will be there, otherwise you could be wait-listed! Our flight wasn't full, but I would have been pretty upset if it was! Luckily, I was rereading the driving directions when I saw that little gem.

We went for the morning flight in order to avoid some of the bumps. That went reasonably well, although the air conditioning did smell of exhaust that started to give us headaches after an :45.

All in all, we are really glad we did it.

Don't forget to tip your pilots! They are trained professionals working very hard for not a lot of money.

review_title: 360 views of the GC!  (But still very loud in a helicopter...)
review_text:
Did this with a friend who was visiting the States from Asia.  Had been to the Grand Canyon myself while in high school (stayed in a cabin with family at the North Rim -- and was still able to enjoy sitting on the veranda overlooking the Canyon, even though we stayed in a cabin, and not at the much pricier NPS Lodge).  Even though my h.s. memories of the GC were wonderful, *nothing* could have prepared me for the amazing views of the Canyon from that helicopter!  Absolutely LOVED it!

4-star rating, and not 5-star, due to the unbelievably LOUD noise level of the chopper's blades -- even though all 10-12 of the passengers were wearing Scenic Airlines' "special headphones" (supposedly to "block out noise"!).  They didn't play music through our headphones on our trip -- but *maybe* after Scenic heard that not all passengers wanted gorgeous views with all that racket they added the music to help "cover" -- a nice idea.

We each paid for a RT ticket -- from the more local Las Vegas airport to the GCA ("Grand Canyon Airport"), stayed overnight, but the flight left very early in the morning, so there really wasn't much time for hiking, etc.  Only wish we had taken video cameras, like many of the other passengers had done!

review_title: Be prepared for lot of waiting around at the canyon
review_text: We went on the plane-helicopter-riverboat tour. This tour was not very well organised at all. The individual aspects on their own were great but put together as a tour, it was poorly organised and we were left extremely disappointed.  Everything up until we reached the canyon airport was great, once we got there it was a complete shambles. We waited for half hour to then be told the helicopter wasnt ready (there werent enough on deck by the sounds). So we were told to take the bus up to the viewing point and get our lunch - it was 9:30am. We were told to be back on the bus at 10:15 to come back to west rim air strip for our helicopter. We had less than one hour to do it all. Even the staff said it wasnt realistic and as it happened one of our group members missed out on lunch as there was a queue for the bathroom. We rushed, got back on time and still had to wait another 20mins for our chopper. Get to the boat platform, queue up again to wait for the boat. 20mins later, finally get on a boat. Nowhere to sit at any waiting places, there were some seats but the number of people far exceeded the number of seats. Spent most of our time at Grand Canyon in an airport or waiting around. The staff tried hard and were very friendly but the system organisation is not good. Papillon operated our helicopter and i would fly direct to GC with them from Boulder City if I could do it over again.

We took the plane ride over the canyon, antelope canyon tour and river raft trip.
It was worth every penny.
The breakfast and lunch provided were more than enough food and packed with lots of options to please everyone.
The plane ride gave me an opportunity to get some great pictures and views of the river not accessible from the rim of the canyon
Antelope Canyon left me speechless....I took 50 pictures.  
The river raft trip was wonderful and our guide John was awesome.  Everybody on our raft really enjoyed themselves.  It was a very safe easy trip.  Only got a few splashes....but we asked for it.  The water was ice cold, 46 degrees I think, but we all jumped in when we stopped for a rest.

My family and I just did Grand Canyon Indian Adventure and Skywalk. In fact, we are still waiting here for a bus to take us back to our hotel- almost 8 hours from when they picked us up this morning (and the tour was only supposed to go 7 hours). By the time we get back to our hotel, we will have spent 5 hours waiting or being shuttled with only 3.5 hours of actual Grand Canyon experience. 

The airplane ride was beautiful, but the plane was not air conditioned as advertised - an important fact in July heat waves. An intake fan does keep the air moving, but that's all. The pot roast style lunch at Guano Point was unedible although the location was breathtaking.

The Grand Canyon itself is beyond words, and I am glad my children were able to see it. But we felt deceived by the advertising - expecting a much more personal experience. Maybe the helicopter tours are different, but this was not what we were looking for at all.

review_title: Awesome trip less the waiting time
review_text: My hubby and I decided not to miss the Grand Canyon since we are already in Vegas. The trip was booked very last minute, just 1-2 days before when we passed by a store along the strip. We just walked in and was greeted by a friendly lady at the counter. We were initially thinking of going on a coach which cost around US160-170 but that would have taken us abt 15+ hrs for the entire trip. Helicopter is another option but that is way too expensive for us as it costs abt US$380 per pax, hence we were offered a in-between option which is by airplane costing US280 per pax.  This is the most viable option for us as the entire trip is abt 7+hrs and we get to save some time for other plans. Staff were generally quite friendly and organized. Not much fuss but waiting time to board the plane can be cut down. Overall, the experience is gd and no regret.

review_title: TRATAR DE ELEGIR UNA EXCURSION COMPLETA
review_text:
Grand Canyon Airlines, funciona junto con Scenic Airlines, y juntas ofrecen varios tours....
El gran Cañón es inmenso, y un tour simple, no alcanza para poder contemplarlo y valorarlo...Hay que tratar de hacer algo un poco mas completo (aunque cueste un poco mas de dinero)..como bajar al rio en helicoptero, o hacer algun vuelo mas largo, pues sino se corre riesgo de contemplar desde el avión solo un borde del cañon (lo minimo con el viaje desde Las Vegas)....
Un consejo IMPORTANTE, no gasten dinero en incluir en su tour el GRAND CANYON SKYWALK (el puente transparente en forma de herradura) pues no merece ni el tiempo ni el dinero...No dejan tomar fotografias, y ni siquiera está sobre el Cañón propiamente dicho, sino sobre una grieta lateral...Desde Guano Point (que es una parada de cualquiera de todos los tours que se ofrecen) hay vistas gratuitas muchisimo mejores

I thought the tour was great. My husband thought it left something to be desired.  We had a buy one-get one deal, so I think it was definitely worth the money. You get to see Lake Mead, Hoover Dam and the edge of the Grand Canyon. They promise four hours from hotel pickup to drop off and that was exact almost to the minute.  They said the tour would be 70 minutes and it was 60, but I felt like it was enough.  We got to see new sights and that's what travel is all about.  My husband felt that the tour was not long enough and that we didn't get to see things close enough or enough of the Grand Canyon. Overall though, it was really enjoyable.

Our family did the Canyon River Adventure over the Memorial Day holiday weekend.  It was a very long, but fun day.  It was exactly 12 hours from the moment our plane left the ground until we arrived back at the airport.  My husband and I had no problem getting out 10 and 15 year old daughters to bed that night.  In fact we all slept 12 hours we were so tired.  The tour was well organized, and worth every cent.  Upon check in at the airport we were served a huge boxed breakfast, too much to eat at once.  We took the extra leftover items for snacks later.  High energy adventure requires food to fuel the body, which they provided plenty.  Bring your cameras, sunscreen, something to cover your mouth/nose while exploring Antelope Canyon, secured sun hats and protective sunglasses that will help prevent sand in your eyes.  When boarding the airplane, try to get a seat on the left side because most of the canyon is visible from the left side.
I suggest protective lens for your camera during the walk through Antelope Canyon, as sand can ruin a camera easily.  I'd also wear a quality face mask or a scarf to prevent inhaling the dust.  Despite being told you won't get wet on the raft trip, you can expect to get wet.  We got soaked, but it felt good.  Mostly everyone slept most of the bus ride back.

review_title: Airplanes fly when copters get cancelled
review_text: We did a plane tour over the canyon with Grand Canyon Airlines out of the nearby airport right outside the park entrance. We had scheduled a helicopter tour with Papillion but it was cancelled due to high winds without any notice even though i heard later they had been canceling all week.. The plane was cheaper and a very smooth ride.. I was also disappointed to learn copters and planes can't fly below the level of the canyon inside the park so I wouldn't have been able to land at the bottom of the canyon anyway unless I had taken a copter tour from Vegas or at the skywalk that fly over and Inside landing in the canyon. GC Airlines was very professional and I was impressed with them. They also had a nice gift shop. The tour was narrated in various languages over headsets. The only downfall was thelackofpersonalinteraction with the pilot..

The airport was very organized and I loved the views over Grand Canyon but both of my daughters got sick from the gas fumes on the plane. There must have been some exhaust back firing. Since we didnt have time for major hiking this was an excellent overview of the canyon and more reasonable than the helicopter ride. I would recommend it but bring a napkin to cover your nose.

I planned a trip to the Grand Canyon for our family of 10 for Ap.,2013. I knew that we wanted to experience an airplane ride over the Canyon. I found Grand Canyon Airlines online. I called and spoke to the booking agent named Monty and told him of our needs. He suggested the  Grand Discovery tour which turned out to be perfect. He also said that he would see that a complimentary shuttle was sent to the Maswik Lodge to pick us up. All our plans went off perfectly and I have Monty to thank. If you plan an airplane ride over the Canyon this company is the one to use. Thanks for helping to make our 50th anniversary trip so memorable.

review_title: Great Views of the Grand Canyon
review_text: We booked the visionary tour online and found it to be great value for money. We were picked up and dropped back at our hotel and the check in at Boulder City was rapid. The pilot was very friendly and the 1 hour flight allowed us to get some great views of the Grand Canyon, Hoover Dam and Lake Mead.

review_title: Superb aerial views of the Canyon
review_text:
We went on the Visionary Air Tour. The pick-up from the hotel was punctual and the check-in was efficient. The flight itself which was a bit over an hour was great although there was some turbulence, which was expected given the size of the plane.  
We had amazing views of the Grand Canyon as well as the Hoover Dam. We could get audio commentaries via headphones but the commentaries were not very detailed or extensive. Still, the aerial views more than made up for that. We were sent back to the hotel again via the shuttle and all in all, we spent a bit over 4 hours for the tour which left us with plenty of time to do other things in Vegas, which was the main reason why we took the flight rather than a bus tour to Grand Canyon which would have otherwise taken 14 hours! 
Overall, it was a great experience and a time efficient way to enjoy Grand Canyon.

review_title: Great scenery but the customer service needs some improvement
review_text:
Overall I'm glad I did this ride. It is a wonderful 70 minute flight into one of nature's great wonders. Grand Canyon Airlines runs this particular trip out of Boulder but they will pick up at your Vegas hotel. A nice plus.

Once you get there it is a bit of a busy environment because they're running helicopter tours out of the small terminal too. But it is fairly straightforward. You get a pink or blue sticker that tells you which group you're with.

They are very keen to herd you around like cattle at this point and I guess with the volume they do I see why. But they also insist on taking your pic with the pilot whether you want it or not. This is supposedly an optional thing you buy for $20 as a souvenir when you come back.

Why is this done? I say it's so they can have a photo record of you. Because if it was optional you could just hop on the plane without doing this if you didn't want to have a pic. They should just tell you that upfront. That it's for i.d. and record keeping purposes! Minus some points for this.

And after your flight takes of you'll find that the Grand Canyon is going to amaze, overwhelm and just plain have your jaw dropping once you are flying over it. They spend quite a bit of time over the various parts of the canyon and there is an audio message you can listen to for background info.

Some bad news for single travellers. You are likely to end up over the wing strut which basically blocks all decent views for photos down into the scenery. Instead of putting me in a single row seat up front they went and stuck me over the strut.

They could have put either one of two families with kids across an entire row and let me have a decent window seat as a solo traveller. The child behind me wasn't even interested in the view and really wasted her window seat. Yes I know they have to weight and balance these airplanes but I'm not a large man. Minus some more points for that.

When you come back you hop on their shuttle back to town. But in the ensuing blabber about telling you how to walk back to the terminal, they DON"T tell you have to check back in at the desk to get a boarding pass for the shuttle!!! Inexcusable.

I was left wondering what I should do and just thought I'd hop on a shuttle going back, and one of their shuttle drivers rudely told me I couldn't ride on a bus going back to Vegas because I didn't have a bus pass!

Not a good ending to a pleasant flight. Overall this attraction lost a lot of points because of these simple glitches that could have easily been prevented from happening... and I rate it as average to poor for customer service issues.

We took the Grand Canyon Deluxe tour to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.  The view from the plane was amazing.  The canyon is much more grand at the South Rim vs the West Rim.  The bus picked us up for a 15 minute trip to the National Park where we were dropped off for 1.5 hours at the first stop.  It was cold so we were glad for the heated restaurant and gift shop!  We had plenty of time to take pictures before heading to the next stop.  Our bus driver was great and very knowledgeable about the canyon, thanks Bob!  The flight back was a little bumpy due to wind and going to a lower elevation, but the pilots were great!  Well worth the time and money.  I highly recommend this tour!

I assumed the ride would be somewhat turbulent because the plane is small (I believe it seats less than 30) but it was so smooth that I fell asleep.  We were told that in April and May it does get very bumpy and a lot of people often get sick though.

The audio doesn't offer much so don't expect a detailed audio tour.  They offer Bose headphones to help mute the noise (very loud).

We booked the Grand Voyager tour as we were looking for a trip that included as much as possible for a reasonable price.  It was difficult to decide between the many companies that offer tours but we were very happy with this tour.  We chose an early flight time of between 6-7am but didn't realise this would mean a 4.50am pick up from our hotel! The pilots and staff were very good and we got to experience the Canyon from an aeroplane, helicopter and boat as well as both Eagle and Guano points.  My only criticism would be that there is not very much communication from the staff about how the tour will go/your itinerary.  It would be helpful if you were given a little more information on this when you arrive.

We did the flight to the Grand Canyon, helicopter ride, boat trip, BBQ then flight back, with shuttle bus to and from the hotel. It all ran smoothly and the staff were very friendly and professional. I would have liked a bit more communication on what would be happening and when, and the BBQ was pretty standard but the scenery is amazing, and that's what we went to see. It's pricey, and I would probably skip the skywalk having experienced it. The boat trip was fantastic though, and its great fun to go in a helicopter. You can buy pictures from the trip but these are expensive so take your own where you can!

I didn't have a lot of time, still wanted to see nature's wonder called Grand Canyon.i booked this trip for 169USD and it was more than I expected. We were transported to boulder municipal airport from our hotel by the airline very comfortably. Our plane was a 17 seater Canada made vista liner with huge windows for full view.

Our pilots were friendly and expert on flying this sector. Plane has pre recorded commentary but you won't hear a lot foot due engine's noise.

This flight gives great view of Hoover dam and a small section of Grand Canyon. It's it for you if you want to spend time in or around Grand Canyon.

I strong recommendation for people short on time still wanting to have a flavor of Hoover dam, Colorado river and Grand Canyon.

This is a do not miss!  The service is impeccable, the staff pleasant and knowledgable and the views tremendous. Bus from your hotel to Bolder City, airplane ride to the South Rim (about an hour of spectacular views including Hoover Dam) and a helicopter ride over the canyon.  Then two hours of sight seeing at the lodge before returning back to Vegas.

we took the grand canyon airlines tour of the south rim just yesterday. the wing was gusting at 40 mph. now, we booked this tour some 2 weeks ago, but due to the bad weather for flying, the company, thought of cancelling it and because it was just my husband and i for the flight. guess what happened, they took us up for the tour. it was cloudy, windy, foggy and the ride was too bumpy the moment the plane took off. even on a foggy, cloudy day-the sights were still incredibly beautiful. the service i think was impeccable, and that is Grand Canyon Airlines not scenic airlines. take it, it is well worth it.

Pick up at the hotel in Las Vegas was right on time.  A 25 minutes drive to Boulder City and then an hour flight to Grand Canyon.  The view from the plane as you fly over Hoover Dam and Lake Mead is spectacular.  We had head phones with a great explanation of the geological wonder that we were viewing. Upon arrival they swiftly bus you up to various places on the South Rim, give you a more than adequate box lunch, and then lots of time to view the canyon and the Colorado River.The return to Vegas was just as peaceful.  Great limo drivers, pilots, guides and bus driver in the National Park.

We took an all day "air, river float & canyon combination tour".  As of July 2012 they called it the Grand Canyon River Adventure.  5:45 am to about 6:30 pm.  A very looong day.  We enjoyed the air tour.  We enjoyed the river float in Glen Canyon. We hated almost everything to do with the rest of the tour.   

Our tour started at the south rim airport with a small plane air tour of the canyon.  We enjoyed it although in retrospect we also decided that a helicopter might have been preferable.  But we saw the canyon from the air and that's really cool.

The airplane took us to the Page, AZ airport where we were told we would be picked up for a tour of Antelope Canyon, perhaps the best of the slot canyons in the area.  We waited about 25 minutes, which was far too long.  Like they didn't know when to expect us?  

Eventually we were picked up at the airport by an extremely rude driver.  He almost left half the tour because when he called for us we didn't hear him and evidently that pissed him off.  Great attitude.  We were loaded on human trailers that had no shocks for a very uncomfortable ride to Antelope Canyon.  The canyon itself was interesting although our guide didn't have much to tell us except where to take pictures.  Then we're loaded back onto the uncomfortable trailers and dropped off in town at a hiking goods/gift shop retail location to wait for our ride to the river float.  

Here's where it got really irritating.  We waited almost 1 1/2 hours at the store and I was getting angrier by the minute.  Far too many people milling around in a very small space. The clerks in the store clearly unhappy that we were all in the store, but there was nowhere else to go.  My family was asked twice to wait outside and I refused both times.  It was horribly hot outside.  July in the desert.   Apparently, the wait was to allow us lots and lots of time to buy things.  That always irritates me and it really irritated me on that occasion.  Finally the buses arrive, we're issued box lunches and off we go.  As I said the river float itself was enjoyable.  Glen Canyon is a very slow current so it's a float - not a white water adventure.  Nonetheless, we had a fun guide and the float itself was fun.  

Then off the rafts and onto buses to be driven all the way back to the south rim - about a 90 minute drive if I remember correctly.  That would have been fine except....WE HAD TO STOP AGAIN FOR ANOTHER BUYING OPPORTUNITY!!!.  We're all tired and ready to be back at the hotel, but we're forced to waste another 45 minutes at the Indian tourist junk store on the way back !!   ARRRGGGG!

Save yourself the frustration.  The indian tribe that operates the Antelope Canyon tour does a TERRIBLE job.  Not worth it and those we encountered were unprofessional and rude.  Far too much of your day is wasted in worthless gift shops, and they are not very friendly in those gift shops.  If you want an air tour, take an air tour by itself.  If you want to float Glen Canyon, do that.  It's fun.  Do not take one of these all day combination tours.  Trust me.

review_title: Maybe not as thrilling as a helicopter ride, but cheaper and safer!
review_text:
We chose the GCA Visionary tour based primarily on safety (helicopter accidents @GC are much more common than fixed wing ones) and secondly on price (its a lot cheaper than a helicopter, and you can find a 2-1 voucher on the internet if you look, which works out slightly cheaper than the online discounted price per person).

Firstly I should say that everything ran smoothly. Pickup from hotel was on time, only a short wait at Boulder City Airport and we were off. From my seat I could see the cockpit and assessed (as a former pilot) the pilot and co-pilot (the latter was in charge of the aircraft whilst airborne) to be very professional.The return trip to LV was also prompt.

I very much enjoyed the tour. Alas my partner kept her eyes front for the whole duration because she was too scared to look out of the window! We chose the early morning set off, but I suspect that a later flight might give better lighting for photos and videos.

Okay, the flight could have gone further along the canyon. And whilst you get a good view, it is  perhaps not as great as with a helicopter. But if you are short on time and have a limited budget, but still want to experience the Grand Canyon, then this is a good option.

review_title: Visionary tour not worth the price
review_text:
We went for the Visionary Tour (1 hour flight). The altitude of the flight is too high, the views of Hoover Dam and Grand Canyon aren't that spectacular.

In my opinion, the experience wasn't worth the price.

If I had to go again, I'm pretty sure the helicopter flights are more exciting- although these are much more expensive. I guess you get what you pay for!

review_title: Best views of the Grand Canyon by Plane.
review_text:
We arrived in the grand canyon area just after lunch, we had pre booked the beautiful Grand Motel, upon checking in to the motel we asked about the best flight tour company to take us over the canyon. the staff were very helpful giving us a number of brochures  on companies  that offered both helicopter & plane tours. We took a look at the opinions & decided to choose the Grand Canyon Airlines, Grand Discovery Tour. We walked back to the reception of the motel & asked if they could organise the tour for two adults & two children for the first tour available in the morning of the next day? She asked if I would like to wait & she would do it right away, I said fantastic! Upon contacting the company she said that we where booked on the 8am flight in the morning & gave us directions to the Grand Canyon Airport where we would be departing, told us to be there by 7.30am. Turned out a great place to stay as it was so close to both the airport & only a couple of mile to the National park entrance. 
So up at 6.30 am, ,got dressed & headed to the Grand Canyon Airport to catch the early 8am flight out over the canyon, we arrived on time & we the reservations as fine & the staff handled the arrival in a professional manner, all safety precaution we followed, weighing everyone & all luggage going on the flight. We where hoping to get a window seat to get the clearest photo opportunities, turned out we only have 4 others on our flight, so all folks on the plane had a window seat. The normal safety checks from one of the pilots to all on board, a quick verbal of how to set up your head set & of to the runway.  We had a smooth take off & good weather as we flew out across the canyon in a 16 seater plane for some amazing views of the whole Grand Canyon incredible experience. We had a narrated tour that lasted about 45 mins, We got some wonderful photos & video footage, it really did feel like we where in the air for such a long time, awesome stuff, this is a great way to see the canyon. You do get to see much more of the canyon from the plane & the weather was fine & clear. After the flight we headed back to the Grand Hotel  for breakfast & then of to the National park to  experience the canyon from the ground with a trek down a trail.  Very happy with the Grand Canyon Airlines company & the tour we choose. Cost $120 per adult $100 per  child.   Good value for money.
Fantastic from start to finish. Just fantastic.  Best trip I ever did. Money well spent. Bryan you are a legend. Nothing more to say.

review_title: You DON'T fly over the Grand Canyon, vous volerez à coté
review_text: Jamais nous n'avons volé au-dessus du Grand Canyon, vous avez un 3-4 minutes de vue sur le côté et c'est tout. Prenez l'hélicoptère si vous en avez les moyens.  Perte d'argent avec ce tour à $250.

I chose this tour because 1. short (more time in Vegas)
                                         2.I had a Canyon River tour booked for with the same guys 2 days later.
Remember to confirm the day before.
Travel light. Take water and camera and be prepared for cooler temperature at flight altitude and early morning pick up.
Pick up at the hotel (what a pleasure) was on time.
Check in at Boulder City was smooth and efficient, a comfortable short wait to rest and prepare before the flight.
The only way to appreciate the GRAND in canyon is from the air although you should see it up close as well - I had that planned for later.
I paid extra for window seating and then shut up, sat back and relaxed for a truly stunning experience. Nobody spoke a word during the flight!
The flight crew was highly competent so no worries!
Back at the airport the excited chatter was remarkable and going back to Vegas seemed an anticlimax. Vegas! Anticlimax! How is this possible?

The pilots were very professional (which made you feel safe).  Every seat in the plane had an excellent view (glass all around).  The tour was narrated by headset and the scenery could not be beat.  The ride was smooth and comfortable (great for taking pictures.  The temperature in the cabin was perfect and plenty of leg room.

When my bank saw the Grand Canyon Airlines name on my charges, it issued a fraud alert and blocked any further purchases. I thought this was a mistake on their part, but perhaps this action was warranted, as we feel the services promised by 'Grand Canyon Adventures'
were not the services delivered. Far from it. We saw very little of the Grand Canyon and far too much, 5.5 hours in fact, of the airport gift shop, helioport gift shop, and parking lot. 

1. Of the 8 hours invested in this 'adventure' we spent 2.5 hours in flight, .25 hours or less in the helicopter hovering over one area of the south rim of the Grand Canyon and one hour at the Grand Canyon National Park. Actually 45 minutes viewing the Grand Canyon from the ground, we spent 15 minutes consuming our pitiful excuse for a lunch. The balance, an estimated 5.5 hours was spent...waiting...waiting...waiting... at the airport, heliport, or on the bus/shuttle in the parking lot of the airport, helioport, etc. etc.  

2. On the first flight we were wedged into the small aircraft like sardines. I am a fairly small woman, as was my companion, an average sized man, so it should have been spacious for smaller folks. It wasn't.  No air to speak of, certainly not air conditioned for comfort as advertised, it was horrendously hot and uncomfortable. We could not breath, got an excruciating headache from it and nausea ensured, although we managed not to throw up. And I have never been air sick, never, even in an ultralight. The views and photography were obstructed by the rotar blades, and of course, other people blocking the windows.
The refitting of the aircraft may have benefited their profit margin but it is detrimental to the passengers.

3. During the helicopter flight I was wedged between two large men, one a total stranger, my petite frame squeezed so tight my lungs barely had room to expand. Needless to say it was embarrassing and humiliating. I am a petite female by the way, and don't appreciate the indignity of having any strange man's body that intimate with mine, thanks.  This advertisement is false, actually, this was not the view.  Most of the time on the helicopter was spent flying to the Grand Canyon, not over the Grand Canyon. We hovered over the same portion, turning to see the same view from a different perspective before we flew back to the heliport.

4. During the flight back, we were again crammed into an overcrowded plane, did not sit with my traveling companion at all. There were tiny windows in the plane, not the 'panoramic windows' promised, not much of a view on our side of the plane, and again, nausea ensued, difficulty breathing. Too late to back out when we saw the plane, it was our ride back to the airport...and more waiting. Again, stuffed into too small of a space. 

5. When we asked about the two viewing points we were suppose to be shuttled to at the park, we were told that yes, the brochures says that, but it will depend on the helicopter schedule, shuttle schedule, etc. So we walked to one viewing point, never saw the other, had to hurry back to the shuttle as we were warned we would miss our plane ride home. No one seemed to know who we needed to speak to about the issue, and we were shifted from one person to another.

6. Should perhaps drive to the canyon, do the helicopter ride from there. Could perhaps have more alternatives if you aren't trapped in a situation you have already paid for.

review_title: Da fare una volta nella vita
review_text:
Penso che se vuoi avere una visione diversa diversa del Gran Canyon questo sia un ottimo modo.
Io ho prenotato il volo deluxe in aereo sul Gran Canyon con gita a a terra che comprende la vista di 2 view point.
L'organizzazione è stata ottima, ci sono venuti a prendere col pulmino alle 4:30 del mattino in hotel, ci hanno portato a Boulder, assegnato un aereo e poi via un bel giro fino al loro aereoporto al Gran Canyon! Durante questo giro vedi il lago Mead, la diga e una parte del Gran Canyon.
Poi siamo saliti su un autobus e ci hanno portato a vedere i 2 più belli view point, tempo libero circa 50 minuti al primo e 40 al secondo, ci hanno dato anche il cestino dellla colazione con muffin, yogurt, succo di frutta e barretta di cereali.
Al ritorno nuovo giro in aereo, che è stato ancora più bello che all'andata. Abbiamo sfiorato un temporale e lì ho avuto un po' di paura, ma tutto è andato bene.
Gli aerei sono un po' vecchi ma a me piaceva lo stile americano da Indiana Jones che avevano. I finestrini sono ampi e permettono di fare delle ottime foto, in compenso il rumore dei motori è molto forte, ma tanto si hanno sugli orecchi le cuffie dell'audioguida che in parte lo coprono.
Non lo rifarei perchè è molto costoso, ma secondo me almeno una volta nella vita conviene farlo.

review_title: Great way to see the canyon
review_text: Really enjoyed the scenic view from the air, got some great photos of the trip. This will be a memorable experience. Flight is about 45 minutes and well worth the time

review_title: Great way to see the Grand Canyon and Skywalk
review_text:
When organising our trip to Las Vegas, Alaska and Canada top priority was given to having the best possible day trip to see the Grand Canyon and Skywalk.  With the help of our travel agent, we decided on Scenic Airlines 'Grand Canyon, Indian Adventure - Helicopter, Boat and Skywalk Tour'.
We were picked up from our Hotel (Signature at MGM Grand) at 4.50am by their shuttle and after picking up a few other guests, were on our way to Boulder Airport.  After processing and grouping there, we climbed aboard the 18 seat aircraft for our trip to the Grand Canyon Airport where we were given a boxed lunch to take with us. (Nothing to write home about but it was sufficient to keep us going).  This is a great flight, flying over the Hoover Dam, Lake Mead and the West Rim. 
We were then taken by bus to the Skywalk area, and did the walk !  The views were just majestic.  After the set time, we were then bussed to another viewing area, after which we were taken back to the Grand Canyon Airport to board our Helicopter for the descent into the Canyon.  Wow, what a buzz this flight is.  We are now down in the canyon,  walked down to the Colarado river (via a track and stairways) for our pontoon boat excursion.  It was so quiet and surreal. Being summer time, by the time we returned back to the helicopter pad from the river it was 42deg C. After a short wait, we were back into the helicopter and back up to the airport.  This is such an amazing flight, and should not be missed.
We then flew back to Boulder Airport in the 18 seat aircraft, and returned to Vegas by their shuttle from Boulder.
We found the whole process to be very well organised and professionally planned.  It was not a cheap trip any any means, but if you want to do things properly then you have to pay for it.  It was a once in a lifetime event for us Aussies and one we will never forget.

review_title: Fantastic way to see the Canyon
review_text: We weren't sure whether we wanted the expense of a flight over the Grand Canyon, but decided to check it out.  Wow this is a great way to see and experience the Canyon.  We took an anti clockwise loop around the whole place and it was just fabulous.  It took 40-45 mins.  The plane was small, but it meant we all had a great window seat.  And the view was just incredible.  The highlight of our vacation.

Traveling as a family with 3 kids under 12, this was one of the highlights of our vacation.  I booked this trip months in advance, to ensure we got on it.  It was recommended by a friend at work and she raved about the experience.  We had to be at the airport at 6 a.m. for an hour flight to Page, AZ.  Flight was smooth and amazing!  After landing in Page, we were met by Indian guides to tour Antelope Canyon. They definately seemed to be on a time table and were even a bit rushed at time, but the tour lasted from ~8:30 a.m. until they dropped us at the river outfitter's at 10 a.m..  Everyone had huge smiles as we were in the 4-wheel truck and touring the very photogenic canyon.  Not to be missed.   From the river outfitter store, we received a saftey briefing and boarded a bus to the river where we met our river guides and started the smooth water float.  Lunch was provided and there were drinks at any time on the raft.  The guide was fun and knowledgeable.  We pulled out at Lee's Ferry about 2:30 p.m. and boarded the bus to take us back to the Grand Canyon area.  We did one stop at the trading post to stretch our leg and grab a snack, arriving back about 6 p.m.  Everyone in our group loved a certain aspect of the trip- it was all well done and we'd do it again.

review_text: The raft trip portion was great as was our guide.  The bus driver (Gigi) was not good.  She talked the entire trip and was annoying as hell.  She talked about herself and how she liked to shop and told stories about herself that no one gave a damn about.  She acted like we were 5th graders. She kept repeating over and over about no weapons allowed.  We got it. Shutup already. The same with drinking lots of water. Every other sentence ended in "Okay?"  Give a little infomation and let people enjoy the scenery and talk to each other a little Gigi. OKAY?

My husband and I have just returned from a trip to the Southwest.  While we were in the Grand Canyon area we decided to take a small plane over the canyon.  We went with the company Grand Canyon Airlines.  This was such a wonderful experience.  We had been to the Grand Canyon and viewed it from the rim many years ago.  I really didn't think that this would be that great.  Boy, was I wrong.  The plane is quite small, but you can see out of both side windows.  They gave us earphones and they played the most beautiful music just as we approached the canyon.  When we were over the canyon I was so overwhelmed by the beauty that I cried.  We had a wonderful female pilot and the flight was very easy.  I would certainly recommend that if you are going to the Grand Canyon that you take the time to view it from the air, either by helicopter or small plane.

review_title: A wonderful way to view the Grand Canyon & Colorado River
review_text:
We booked the River Adventure with Scenic Airlines, which consisted of a flight over The Grand Canyon, a jeep trip to Antelope Canyon, and then a gentle river raft down the Colorado River. 
The day started at The Grand Canyon Airport around 6 am for check in.  We were then given the included continental breakfast in a transportable container which included cereal bar, muffins, yogurts, fruit, cheese & crackers - better than expected! We then took a flight across the east side of the Grand Canyon up to Page, which lasted approx 50 mins. It was a very smooth flight with amazing views. We then took a coach for a 15 min ride to the Jeep for a tour of Antelope Canyon, which was also amazing. A further short coach ride took us to the River raft, which took us on a gentle ride through Glen Canyon along the Colorado river. This took approx 3 hours and we stopped at a beach area halfway through to eat the lunch provided, which again was better than I expected. There was then a 3 hour guided tour coach ride back through the Grand Canyon to the airport, arriving back about 5.30pm. It was a long day, but a great way to experience the areas visited. There were plenty of restroom stops and a little waiting around, mainly due to people taking the tour arriving late. Overall it was a very smooth, and well organised day.

review_title: Spectacular day, varied and accessible to nearly any age or ability
review_text:
Instead of hours on a mule to reach the canyon floor, we are darn glad we opted to do this.  It is an adventure.  

For departure, go to Grand Canyon Airport (not heliport!)  We recommend sitting on the right side of the airplane for the great views of the canyons; plan to bring extra food, water and reading material or games.  Plenty of toilets available on the entire trip.  The river is easy but it is spectacular. Young children might find the ride home too long unless they are nappers. People with difficulty walking could enjoy the day.  The outfitters will accommodate wheelchairs as long as the chair can be folded up and there is someone to push the chair.  A chair would not be great in Antelope Canyon, however.  This is a flat, easy walk but the floor is sand - very tough on wheels.  But the flight and the raft (and fun short bus ride from Page to Glen Canyon Dam) are fabulous.

Our river guide, Meghan (?), was splendid - a biologist, historian, naturalist and fine storyteller. We loved this portion and were never bored even though there are no rapids here.  You just float past magnificent and varied scenery.  Bring extra batteries, binoculars would be fun, dress in layers - we had three seasons in one outing.  You definitely need sun protection (even in April!) and the hikes are so easy you need no special footwear.  

Once on Colorado River there are three stops, one is a splendid sandy beach.  You might to wear like a swim suit or fast dry clothes on a hot day. Each stop has toilets.

There are some waits throughout the day and a very long ride home on a motorcoach from Lee's Ferry back to GC Airport  but you will see how the Navaho people live .  Their reservation borders the road home.  You can shop for fine Navaho art and crafts at the Cameron Trading Post Galley on the ride home.  Just avoid the junk in the large, also junky, gift shop. The food options at the Trading Post are bleak - mostly junk food.

Trips can be cancelled due to weather issues so be sure to confirm the day before and understand if winds get too strong you may not be able to go.  Both days before and after our trip were cancelled.

 The return trip takes you into the National Park at the east entrance, Desert View.  However, the bus home does not stop at any of the lookouts once in the park.  But you will be glad, ready to get back to your car and your hotel.  

Though the trip seems expensive it is worth every penny.  It was a great deal more fun and interesting than sitting on a mule.

I booked the Grand Canyon River Adventure tour through The Grand Canyon Air tours and let me say we loved every bit of it. This was our first trip to the Grand Canyon and wanted to explore it through a tour. My family and i enjoyed all of it. From the plane ride to the antelpoe canyon and river ride it is a complete awsome package for a first time visit.

i found a coupn on the internet for buy one get one so that was nice call to make a reservatin and was charge and additional $50 FOR TAXES AND FEES, seemed a little pricey questioned represntatative about the additional $50 Iwas just told it was taxes and fees but not what kind

We arrived at the airport on your shuttle on time and were suppose to take off on the airplane at 9:30a.  We boarded the plane along with everyone else and the pilot noticed that a guage was not showing the proper reading.  He asked us to deplane and they would have it looked at (probably a bad guage).  The guage wasn't bad and there was something wrong so they sent another plane over about 10:30a.  We boarded that plane and the pilot started the engine (I was in 1st seat behind pilot).  He was concerned about a reading on a guage and took out the manual and checked it and discussed with co-pilot.  Then he gave throttle and let it come back and I could see the guage in question which was reading 30psi less than the other engine.  He then looked at the manual again and said to the co-pilot "it looks like its at minimum acceptable" and we proceeded to take off.
 
During the entire flight the pilot was pointing to the guage and speaking to the co-pilot and was visibly concerned.  We went to land and the aircraft swayed more than normal and we touched down.  Upon getting to our parking space he opened his door and told the ground crew to have maintenance come to check the engine as he felt there was something wrong and pointed to the guage.
 
We got into a bus and took off to our 1st destination (we were told there would be 3) and we were allowed 30 minutes at that location (a lodge) and were given a box lunch and told to enjoy.  We didn't have time to do much.
 
We then got to the 2nd location and had 30 minutes and were told that was the last location we would visit.
 
We headed back to the airport and I asked the attendent when our plane was to take off and she indicated that our plane was 'sick' and they were sending another one.  They offered us a free drink for the wait (about 1.5 hrs).   She didn't know how long the wait would be.
 
So - we waited 3 hours for planes (each way), went to only 2 destinations and were seriously late coming back to Las Vegas where we had made evening plans.
 
We are not satisified with $50 credit for each ticket.
 
We are requesting a complete refund as we felt we were put into a dangerous situation and we were completely stressed out on our 'once in a lifetime trip to the Grand Canyon'.
 
We took your service because we didn't want to take 13 hours using the bus and paid the premium.  We got on our shuttle at 7:45a and returned after 5:30p.  We were supposed to get back at 3:30p.  We would never take your service again

Dont take a helicopter - take the 50 minute flight by plane and see the Canyon the best way you can.
We have done the helicopter flight and it just does not compare with the airplane trip, you see so much more.
Also the staff are very friendly and helpful, from online booking to  getting you on and off the plane.
We also mislaid a camera on the plane and after contacting them the staff not only found the camera but had it returned to our hotel.
Talk about service above and beyond.............................
Very highly recommended.

review_title: Canyon River Adventure – Plane, 4x4 Vehicle, River Raft, Motor Coach
review_text:
I booked the “Canyon River Adventure” tour directly with Grand Canyon Airlines but you can also book thru Papillon Grand Canyon Helicopters, GrandCanyon.com, or Xanterra Parks & Resorts. This tour departs from the Grand Canyon Airport in Tusayan (8 miles south of Grand Canyon Village / Grand Canyon South Rim).

This comprehensive tour is operated by the partnership of 3 companies: 
GRAND CANYON AIRLINES - flight over canyon in fixed wing 19-seat Vistaliner plane with over-sized windows; 
ANTELOPE SLOT CANYON TOURS – four-wheel drive vehicle tour to Antelope Canyon; 
COLORADO RIVER DISCOVERY - 15-mile smooth water float trip on a river raft, beginning at Glen Canyon Dam and ending at Lee’s Ferry. 

At the end of the full-day excursion, a motor coach returns you back to Grand Canyon Airport.

Tour Description and Video: http://youtu.be/_Qi2Lpemuyc

Tips for hot days:  Sunblock, wide brim hat, a small towel or bandana to soak in river and wrap around neck. Store all electronic devices in a waterproof bag. My boyfriend’s cell phone and iTouch were both ruined by a splash of river water on his backpack. The seats and floor of the raft can also become wet with small puddles of water.

If you are prone to motion sickness, consider taking a half tablet of Bonine (or similar antiemetic) before the plane tour. Wind gusts over the canyon can occur, making the ride intermittently bumpy.

The 2-mile journey on the 4x4 vehicle to Antelope Canyon is very bumpy and dusty. You will travel over an unpaved road in thick sand. Those with back problems and contact lense wearers should beware. Antelope Canyon is a natural marvel and a photographer’s oasis.
Poorly organized, treat you like a group of cows, old and even dangerous planes and hellicopters. Never again.

review_title: Awesome and great way to see the Grand Canyon and Hoover Dam
review_text:
My husband and I booked a Visionary Flight from Grand Canyon Airlines, its the cheapest flight.  Plan on about 4 hours round trip from the hotel. We were picked up at 6:30AM, right on time, in a clean shuttle bus with a very chatty driver. We were driven to Boulder City Airport, about a 30 minute drive.  We checked in, waited about 30 minutes, just long enough to have a cup of coffee and a donut, then were loaded onto another bus, and driven out to the tarmac. 

NOTE:  there are very clean rest rooms in the airport, but NONE on the plane!

Each person/couple poses with the pilot, then receives a seat assignment and boards. The plane seats around 20 people, single person on one left, 2 side-by-side on the right.   Windows are oversized for good viewing. headsets are available for up to 4 languages, our flight included English, Korean, and Swedish, each on its own channel.  So, off we go, short flight to Boulder Dam, then over Lake Meade, and finally to the Grand Canyon. Awesome, awe inspiring, there are just not words to describe its majesty viewed from the air.  Total in-air time was about 60 minutes. Then we landed.  You can purchase your photo with the pilot for $20, spend the extra $9 for the video; this is a very slick, professional video of the entire  length of the Colorado River, about 60 minutes long, very very well done.  Then we received a token, went outside, boarded a shuttle. We were driven to a transfer point, got off and transferred to another shuttle, and driven back to the hotel. About 3.5 hours total.

This is not a cheap trip, its going to cost about $150 per person (around $125 plus tax).  The bus tour is around 10 hours total trip, and not much cheaper (about $100/person without tax).  However, if you do the GCA tour in the morning, you are back in Vegas by lunch, and still have the entire afternoon and evening to enjoy.  For $25 more per person, we felt that CGA was the better route, and it was.

Al di la' dal prezzo ( circa 300 dollari a persona) molto dipende dal vostro concetto di visita. Abbiamo scelto la versione delux e abbiamo scoperto che il volo serve solo per portarvi al parco ( da boulder city e non da las vegas) e non per sorvolare il canyon e la tratta in autobus fa due tappe vicine ai ristoranti, la vista da li e' suggestivaok, ma se avete tempo e modo andate in macchina che risparmiate e lo vedete meglio!!!

Our plane was delayed for over an hour coming back from Grand Canyon. without any announcements or explanations as to why and how much longer... I was almost scolded by the lady in charge when I asked when we would be taking off.

When we finally took off and landed in Boulder City, there were no busses to transfer us to Vegas. They told us to wait for another hour! 

When we protested, no one actually took any responsibility and the staff at the desk actually resorted to lies - blaming the weather conditions and technical issues for the delays whereas we had leraned  by then that there were actually waiting for 3 people who didi not show up.

Finally they took us to LV in a shuttle bus that they had initially said did not have the permit to make  trip to LV, on account of no seatbelts.  

We made it to the hotel almost 2 hours later than the announced time and  I missed a 150$, non-refundable massage that I had booked earlier.

Some people in our group took the heli ride to the base of the canyon and were stranded there for an extra hour since the staff kept putting other people ahead of them in the line.

review_title: Poorly organised which lead to not enough time at the rim!
review_text:
We chose Scenic airlines for a tour to the grand canyon because we didn't have the time to drive to it ourselves. BIG MISTAKE! Drive to it yourselves! Do not book a flight, but spend a couple of days there, it's so worth it!

We booked the grand canyon deluxe tour (180 euro's per person, I think that's like 220 dollars) with Scenic air because the itenerary said it was approximately 8 hours  from hotel to hotel (note: Scenic and Papillon are thesame company). So we thought: 2 times a 1.15h flight and 2 times a 1 hour pick up and drop off at the hotels which meant 3 - 3.5 hours at the rim. Maybe that was our mistake for thinking it would be so simple.

We took the 9.15 flight which meant we were picked up at our hotel at 7:45 by a very very cranky busdriver who obviously didn't like his job. We arrived at Boulder airport  one hour and ten minutes later because we had to do pick ups at other hotels. Oke, that's understandable, Las Vegas is a big city. 

When we arrived at the airport we were told that there was construction going on at the rim so there could be some delays when we actually had to enter the parc, but that it wouldn't be at the cost of our time at the rim. So no worries there. So we waited at the aiport untill 9.30 (15 min delay, never understood why) and before boarding we had to take a picture with the pilot (??) so that could be sold to you afterwards. The flight itself was really beautiful with fantastic views of the grand canyon. 

When we entered the parc we were told to hurry to the bus but there was no busdriver... After a while our really nice busdriver (Gigi) arrived and warned us about the construction again. But the bus could just go through the gates without any delays. We were dropped of at a view point with a great lunchbox and were given 55 min. to come back at the bus. After that we went to another view point and were again given 55 min. After that, we thought we were going to yet again a view point, but Gigi told us we were going back to the airport. 

When we were back at Boulder airport we had  to wait half an hour for a bus that would take us back to the hotel. After driving around for an hour and a half dropping everyone off, we had to get out of the bus, go into another bus, and dropp off even more people?! After 2 HOURS driving around we were finally back at out hotel.  That was just not okay.

Would rate poor instead of average, especially after all the delays which had nothing to do with construction but everything with the organisation, but it was kinda our own fault to choose this airline

review_title: Combo trip to south rim was fantastic!
review_text: Grand Canyon Airlines' airplane/land combo trip to south rim was awesome.They picked us up on time from our hotel in Las Vegas.The individual headsets with narration in the airplane were very nice.The grandeur of the canyon can  be fully experienced from the air views.We had asked for vegetarian meals during booking which they failed to provide in the bus portion of the your. Once this lapse was brought to their notice they provided us with veg lunch boxes once we arrived at the airport in grand canyon. Also they refunded 10$ per person for this lapse on their part. So a 5-star to their customer service!!

review_title: Vedi il Grand Canyon e poi muori...di paura
review_text: Ho prenotato in Internet con Papillon Grand Canyon il tour sia in aereo che in pullman, quello che è chiamato Deluxe. Rimando alla recensione su Papillon le considerazioni sull'organizzazione del tour. Riguardo l'aereo, ho dovuto constatare che i velivoli non sono nuovi e non offrono a mio avviso tutte le garanzie per affrontare comunque più di un'ora di volo sul Canyon. La compagnia si vanta di non aver nelle proprie statistiche disastri, ma dovrebbero comunque rinnovare gli aerei che si mostrano piuttosto vecchi. Il Grand Canyon è bellissimo, bellissimo il Colorado, ci tornerei di certo, ma non userei gli stessi aerei

While at the Grand Canyon this July, I booked the family on Grand Canyon Air's Grand Discovery Tour.  Although the view from the air is quite good, I thought that it really didn't add too much to the overall Canyon experience, was very expensive (about $600 for 6 of us) and the very bumpy flight was disturbing to half the family.  I would pass on this tour and save the money the next time around.

review_title: No Trip to Las Vegas Would Be Complete Without It
review_text:
Having booked a week in Las Vegas over the 4th July weekend, one of our top priorities was to get to see the Grand Canyon. We originally planned on hiring a car and driving there, but were put off by the lengthy drive and the idea of a whole day cooking together in the car !
Instead, we decided to look at our options for taking a flight over the Canyon. Taking our place in the human mass that ebbs and flows up and down the Strip, we were occasionally cornered by sales or timeshare agents trying to persuade us to part with more of our overdraft (!) in exchange for a variety of trips, shows and events. We quickly established that booking a flight through these agents was going to cost a minimum of $130 each (around £80 in real money) for a plane trip, and substantially more for a helicopter ride. We also learned the hard way, that it's sometimes difficult to extract yourself from the clutches of these agents, if they get even the slightest sniff of possibility that you might take your wallet or your credit card out. So if you intend speaking to them, you have to be prepared to walk away if you don't want what they're selling !

Once we'd established the 'ball-park' cost of a trip, we returned to our hotel and accessed the internet to compare prices direct. Keeping to our budget, we wanted a short plane ride which wouldn't take up all of our day. After some searching, we found GrandCanyonAirlines.com who have a broad spectrum of both helicopter and airplane options available. Their website is easy to use and their prices are far better than most. We booked 2 tickets online for $94 each (around £60), opting for the early morning (6am) flight. Be warned though - the website allows you to check flight availability for the next day but it doesn't tell you until AFTER you've made your selections, that you have to book at least 3 days in advance !?!?! So don't leave it until the end of your holiday to book in. Having negotiated this minor hurdle, we then discovered that our pick-up time would be at an ungodly 4am ! Not the easiest time in the morning to rise after a night of Mojitos and Margueritas ! !

Anyway, on the day, our pick-up was running 10 or 15 minutes late (no big deal) and after collecting four other couples, the drive to Boulder City airstrip took around 40 minutes. The set up there is pretty good and certainly better than I imagined it might be. They have a fairly new terminal building with a small coffee shop / gift store, and enough seating for most. Each passenger books in and is then weighed, to calculate distribution around the airplane cabin. This was particularly pleasing as it made a mockery of those who had raced off the bus to be first in line, shouldering children and elderly folk out of the way to get the best seats - I'm joking of course but there was a stampede to be first in line ! Outside on the apron were numerous helicopters and around the corner sat the airplanes. Lots of people were arriving from different places for a number of early flights. Unfortunately for us, only 4 of the 8 passengers booked on our plane had managed to drag themselves out of bed for the pick-up, and our flight was cancelled. This is something else to be wary of, although you have no control over it. If they don't have the minimum number on the day, the flight is scrubbed. We were offered alternative flights and chose to return next morning at a slightly later time (so we could get more sleep ! !).

Our pick-up next morning was more eventful - Running late again with another family already on the bus, we were then delayed a further 20 minutes at our hotel while we waited for members of said family to visit the restrooms !  What it is exactly that takes 20 minutes, I'll never know ! ! !  However, this is another drawback of these trips and you should be prepared for the possibility that your pick-up may run very late. It clearly caused some concern with those waiting further along the Strip to be collected. Nonetheless, we still arrived at Boulder in time so there was less time sitting around.

So to the flight. The plane was small and cosy with large viewing windows. The crew were very friendly and accommodating. We had headsets that alternated between playing an audio travel guide with useful information on the area, and a cheesy soundtrack that I reckon was taken from "Blazing saddles" !  The flight was nice and smooth (taking into account the odd airpocket that wouldn't constitute turbulence, but which still caused my other half to attempt to surgically remove my left bicep, using only her fingernails and her teeth ! !) And the Grand Canyon itself... What can I possibly say that far better writers than I, havn't already said...?  It was an experience we'll never forget. It was utterly magnificent. It's impossible to convey the sheer scale and magnitude and it was so humbling to fly over it, through it and around it. Driving to the rim would never have afforded such views, so taking the plane ride was money well spent. It was a fabulous journey which also took in the Hoover Dam and it's new road bridge, as well as Lake Mead.

Would we recommend Grand Canyon Airlines? Definitely. 
Would we fly with them again? Absolutely. In a helicopter next I think !
What should you take? Cameras, spare batteries and memory card, cash (for the coffee shop / gift store), sunglasses, water (it can get pretty stuffy if the bus is full).

We had an amazing experience with Scenic Airlines last week (November 2008).

We took the overnight tour - which included an early pick-up from the hotel (5am!!!), an amazing and incredibly smooth flight at 6:40am from Boulder City airport to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon), a drop off at a viewing point, a rather delicious buffet lunch at a hotel in Tusayan, a visit to an Imaxx theatre to see a film about the Grand Canyon, and then a further drop off at the Bright Angel viewing point (which was very close to out hotel - The Maswik Lodges). We were able to see the Sunset, and in the following morning we had an option to get up and see the Sunrise too (a bus picked us up at 6:30am to take us to a suitable viewing point). This whole trip was excellently organised and run by a group of exrtremely affable and interesting tour guides.

I can't reccommend this trip enough! It was one of the very few companies that offered flights to the South Rim of the Canyon, with an overnight stay in the park itself. Well worth the money!
